report_name: Healthcare Sector Faces Surge in Social Engineering & Vishing Attacks

threat_actors.name: ShinyHunters
threat_actors.description: A notorious threat actor group conducting aggressive voice phishing (vishing) campaigns against the healthcare and pharmaceutical sectors to manipulate employees, compromise credentials, and use operational downtime as an extortion tactic.
threat_actors.goals: Extortion of healthcare and pharmaceutical organizations by threatening operational downtime.

threat_actors.name: The Com
threat_actors.description: An underground cybercrime network linked to the phishing domain my-passkeys[.]com, used in social engineering attacks against the healthcare sector.
threat_actors.goals: Credential theft from healthcare sector employees.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing for Information
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors conducted direct, interactive social engineering over the phone (vishing) to manipulate employees into resetting passwords or MFA.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: Malicious domains hosting phishing kits were used to harvest credentials and MFA tokens after a target was directed to the site during a vishing call.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Attackers gained initial access to organizational networks, VPNs, or cloud applications using credentials stolen through vishing and phishing sites.

attack_patterns.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
attack_patterns.description: Attackers attempted to bypass MFA by tricking users into approving push notifications, a technique known as MFA Fatigue.

identities.name: Health-ISAC member organizations
identities.description: A class of organizations in the healthcare and pharmaceutical sectors targeted by a widespread and systematic social engineering campaign. Over a dozen members were reportedly impacted.

identities.name: Healthcare Sector
identities.description: The healthcare industry was a primary target of a wave of sophisticated social-engineering attacks, with threat actors leveraging the sector's reliance on constant uptime for extortion.

identities.name: Pharmaceutical Industry
identities.description: The pharmaceutical industry was targeted alongside the healthcare sector in a series of vishing and social engineering campaigns.

infrastructure.name: my-passkeys.com Phishing Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: A malicious domain used to host phishing kits designed to harvest credentials and MFA tokens from employees in the healthcare sector. Linked to 'The Com' cybercrime network.

indicators.name: Phishing Domain my-passkeys.com Detection
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Phishing Domain my-passkeys.com DNS Query
id: 7f5a9b1c-8d2e-4f3a-9c1b-6a8d2e4f3a9c
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS queries to the malicious domain my-passkeys.com, which is associated with social engineering campaigns targeting the healthcare sector.
references:
  - https://www.cybersecuritydive.com/news/threat-groups-social-engineering-attacks-healthcare/831383/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-25
tags:
  - attack.t1566.002
  - attack.initial_access
level: high
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|contains:
      - 'my-passkeys.com'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects network traffic to the phishing domain my-passkeys.com, used in vishing campaigns against the healthcare sector.

indicators.name: Help Desk Initiated Password Reset
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Help Desk Initiated Password Reset
id: 4b1c8d2e-9c1b-4f3a-8d2e-6a8d2e4f3a9c
status: experimental
description: 'Detects help desk tickets indicating a password reset was initiated via a phone call, which could be part of a vishing attack. This requires correlation with authentication logs.'
references:
  - https://www.cybersecuritydive.com/news/threat-groups-social-engineering-attacks-healthcare/831383/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-25
tags:
  - attack.t1598
  - attack.t1078
level: medium
logsource:
  category: application
  product: generic
detection:
  selection:
    keywords:
      - 'password reset'
      - 'MFA reset'
      - 'initiated via phone call'
      - 'user reported urgent need'
  condition: all of selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate urgent password resets initiated by phone.
indicators.description: Detects patterns in help desk logs that may indicate a password reset initiated via a vishing phone call, as described in the hunting hints.
